_comment: Consumed by deploy.mjs — run it with `npm run deploy`.
STAGING until the cutover. quickeasysoftware.com is still served by WordPress via a
CloudFront distribution in the second AWS account; the hosted zone lives there too,
alongside live systems (bos-api, elsumo-api, the bospro/bosent tenants, docs, mail,
portal, app). The cutover moves the apex + www aliases onto our distribution and
repoints two records — it does NOT migrate the zone.
With no CloudFront there is no create-invalidation step, so a long immutable TTL
is unsafe for files that change in place under the same name. Images are immutable
(a changed image gets a new filename); css/js revalidate every 5 minutes.
Once cloudfrontDistributionId is set, deploy.mjs invalidates on every deploy and
the css/js group can move to the immutable value.

notes: The exclude list keeps dev artifacts off the public endpoint. Note that adding an
--exclude does NOT remove a file already in the bucket: sync applies filters to the
destination too, so --delete skips excluded keys. Anything already published has to
be removed with an explicit `aws s3 rm <key>`.
Every page canonicalises to https://quickeasysoftware.com/..., which is what keeps
the public staging endpoint from competing with the live site in search.
